article.Citation/Title: Costello, C. G. (1969). An evaluation of aversion and LSD therapy in the treatment of alcoholism. Canadian Psychiatric Association Journal, 14(1), 31-42.
article.EligibilityNote: Titled 'Review'; Costello critically synthesizes published aversion-therapy and LSD-therapy studies for alcoholism (Lemere & Voegtlin, Sanderson et al., Smart et al., Table II) without conducting original enrollment, an assigned regimen, or prospective outcome assessment of his own. Fails criterion (a): not a clinical trial the author conducted.

ae_events.Description: Respiratory paralysis (apnea) after succinylcholine injection during aversion conditioning; duration 63-150 sec, mean 90.4s (SD 24s), n=15 pilot patients.
Post-conditioning physiological disturbances after succinylcholine: irregular heart rate, sudden muscle twitches, fluctuating GSR baseline, persisting for some time post-session.
Diarrhea, described as mostly mild, associated with emetic-drug (emetine-based) aversion therapy across the reviewed literature.
Sinusitis reported as a side effect of emetic-drug aversion therapy in the reviewed literature; frequency and course not detailed.
Cystitis reported as a side effect of emetic-drug aversion therapy in the reviewed literature; frequency and course not detailed.
Prostatitis reported as a side effect of emetic-drug aversion therapy in the reviewed literature; frequency and course not detailed.
Neuromuscular disturbances, described as light to moderate, reported with emetic-drug aversion therapy in the reviewed literature.

article.Outcome: This article is a narrative review with no original trial and no single stated primary outcome of its own; it synthesizes improvement/abstinence rates from six LSD studies (Table II, mean 75% improvement, range 50-93%) and multiple aversion-therapy studies, but designates no single primary comparison of its own. Coded '.' rather than selecting one reviewed study's statistic, which would misattribute another trial's effect size to this record.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic is paired with a primary outcome of this article's own; individual reviewed studies' statistics (e.g., Table I's chi-squared values for Madill et al.'s craving-reduction comparison) belong to those separate trials, not to this review. Coded '.'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: No original analyzed sample exists; the article synthesizes studies with heterogeneous Ns (145 in the unpublished Saskatchewan report, 10/10/10 in Smart et al. 1966, 68 in O'Reilly & Funk 1964, etc.). Coded '.'.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: The article is a narrative critical review, not an original trial. Only the objective (evaluate the aversion-therapy and LSD-therapy literature for alcoholism) is stated. There is no original design, setting, eligibility criteria, intervention protocol, comparator, outcome measures, sample-size/power statement, randomization, blinding, statistical methods, results, harms assessment, or funding/COI disclosure for an original study, because no such study was conducted by the author; the review's synthesis of others' results and harms is not the same as this article describing its own trial's results/harms.

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 3 (cannot be determined) because no single trial result belongs to this article. The author is skeptical about aversion therapy ('no good evidence that aversion procedures are particularly effective') and cautious/mixed about LSD (75% mean improvement across largely uncontrolled comparisons, but the one adequately controlled study, Smart et al. 1966, found no LSD advantage over ephedrine or time). No single directionality is attributable to 'this study'.
article.Clincial Trial YN: Coded 0 to match the eligibility screen: the article is a narrative review of others' trials, not a trial the author conducted himself.
article.RandomizationYN: Coded 3 (does not apply): no original participants were enrolled or randomized by the author; this presupposes an original trial that does not exist here (distinct from the single-arm-trial boundary case, where a trial exists but lacks randomization).
article.BlindingYN: Coded 3 (does not apply): no original study procedure exists to blind.
article.Double+Blind: Coded 3 for the same reason as BlindingYN; no contradiction since BlindingYN is also 3, not 0.
article.Comparator: Coded 3 (does not apply): the author ran no comparison of his own; comparator arms discussed (e.g., ephedrine, placebo, no-treatment) belong to the individual reviewed trials.
article.PrimaryCare: Coded 0: unlike randomization/blinding/comparator, this asks a straightforward question answerable directly from the text regardless of whether an original trial exists -- nothing in the article ties any aspect to primary-care settings or providers.
article.Power: Coded 0: statistical power is a topic a review could discuss even without an original trial (e.g., as a critique of the reviewed studies), but this article never raises it anywhere.
article.Retention (%): Coded '.': no original enrolled/randomized sample exists to compute a completion percentage for.
article.MediatingYN: Coded 3 (does not apply): no original trial exists for the author to have run a formal mediation analysis on; this presupposes an original study with a measured intermediate variable and an indirect-effect test, which is absent here for the same reason as RandomizationYN/Comparator. No mediator was ever measured because no original study was conducted.
article.ModeratingYN: Coded 3 (does not apply): same reasoning as MediatingYN -- no original trial or measured candidate moderator exists for the author to have tested for an interaction effect. (The article does discuss candidate moderators, such as employment status and personality traits, as topics future research should investigate, but names no formal moderation test conducted on any data of the author's own.)
article.HypothesisTestReportedYN: Coded 3: there is no primary outcome/comparison belonging to this article's own (nonexistent) trial to test, consistent with Outcome='.'. Individual reviewed studies report their own inferential tests (e.g., Table I's chi-squared=5.123, non-significant, for Madill et al.'s craving-reduction comparison; Smart et al.'s non-significant LSD-vs-ephedrine-vs-control comparison), but those tests belong to those separate trials, not to this review's own primary comparison, which does not exist.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: Coded 3 (does not apply): the author enrolled no participants of his own, so there are no inclusion/exclusion criteria to state.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: Coded 3 (does not apply): no original outcome measurement was performed by the author.
article.Funding/COI YN: Coded 0: the only provenance note is that the paper was based on a 1967 conference presentation; no funding source or conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere in the text.
article.BaseStatus: Coded '.', never a number: this is a review with no participant sample, so the severity-of-condition concept does not apply and the closed-enum field takes '.'.
article.Age_Median: Coded '.', never a number, for the same reason as BaseStatus: no participant sample exists to have a median/mean age.
article.PercentFem: Coded '.': no original sample exists to report a sex/gender composition for.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Coded '.': no original sample exists to report race/ethnicity composition for.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 3 (does not apply): no original participants were enrolled or described by the author.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Coded '.': no original study population exists. (The author's affiliation is the University of Calgary, Canada, but that is the author's institution, not a study population, and this field is reserved for the actual study sample's country.)
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 3 (does not apply): no original recruitment occurred.
article.InterventionDescription: Coded '.': the article discusses several distinct interventions (emetic-drug aversion therapy, succinylcholine aversion therapy, electric-shock aversion therapy, and single-dose LSD ranging roughly 200-800 microgram across cited studies) rather than one protocol of the author's own; no single description applies.
article.InterventionTherapy: Coded 3 (does not apply): no intervention of the author's own was administered.
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 1, consistent with SafetyReported='Y'. Although the author conducted no original trial, the text explicitly relays adverse/side-effect information from the aversion-therapy literature it reviews (succinylcholine-induced apnea and post-conditioning physiological disturbance; emetic-drug side effects: diarrhea, sinusitis, cystitis, prostatitis, neuromuscular disturbances). Per the prompt's cardinal rule against understating harm, this content is coded as harms reporting rather than discarded as 'safety never assessed', even though it is second-hand (drawn from cited studies) and concerns the non-psychedelic aversion-therapy agents rather than LSD specifically -- the LSD-therapy section of the article contains no comparable AE detail.
article.Followup in months: Coded '.': the article cites many different follow-up windows across different reviewed studies (e.g., Madill et al. 3 weeks/3 months, Clancy et al. 1 year, O'Reilly & Funk 2-34 months, Jensen & Ramsay various) with no single follow-up duration belonging to this article itself.
article.BehaviorChangeMeasured: Coded 1: the article extensively reports on drinking-behavior and craving outcomes measured in the reviewed literature (Table I's 'Reduction in Craving'; avoidance/aversive-response behaviors). Judgment call: reflects outcome domains covered in the surveyed literature, not an outcome measured by Costello's own (nonexistent) study.
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: Coded 1: physiological measures (heart rate, GSR, apnea duration) from the succinylcholine studies are reported. Same judgment call as BehaviorChangeMeasured.
article.ReductionMeasured: Coded 1: Table I reports a distinct 'Reduction in Craving' outcome (partial behavioral reduction, not full cessation) drawn from Madill et al.
article.CessationMeasured: Coded 1: complete abstinence ('completely abstinent', 'totally dry') is extensively discussed as an outcome across both the aversion-therapy and LSD-therapy sections.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 1: relapse/return-to-drinking is explicitly tracked in the reviewed follow-up data (e.g., the Saskatchewan report's 'occasional relapses ... becoming fewer and of shorter duration').
article.MentalHealthChangeMeasured: Coded 0: no depression/anxiety/well-being scale outcome is discussed anywhere as a measured domain; anxiety and personality traits are discussed only as hypothesized predictors of conditionability, not as a measured mental-health outcome.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: Coded 0: no quality-of-life instrument or outcome is discussed anywhere in the text.
article.Implementation Outcome: Coded 0: no feasibility/acceptability/fidelity/reach/adoption/sustainability outcome is discussed anywhere in the text.
article.MortalityMeasured: Coded 0: mortality is never addressed as an outcome or otherwise anywhere in the article; treated as 'not covered' consistent with the other undiscussed outcome domains (MentalHealthChangeMeasured, QualityOfLifeMeasured, Implementation Outcome), rather than '.' since its absence from the text is itself informative for this review's scope.
article.LSD: Coded 0, not 1, despite LSD being the article's central topic: the substance flags are intervention flags for the study being coded (the author's own study), and Costello administered no LSD himself -- LSD was administered only in the separate trials he reviews (Table II).
article.Mescaline: Coded 0 for the same reason as LSD: mescaline appears only as an alternative arm in one reviewed trial (Smith 1958, '200 or 300 microgram LSD or 0.5 gr. mescaline'), not as something the author administered.
article.SafetyReported: Coded 'Y': the article explicitly reports AE-type content relayed from the aversion-therapy literature it synthesizes (see HarmsAssessed rationale), so it is not silent on safety, even though the reporting is second-hand and concentrated on non-psychedelic aversion agents rather than LSD.
article.AnyAEReported: Coded 'Y', consistent with SafetyReported='Y' and the non-empty ae_events array.
article.NumDistinctAEs: Counted 7 distinct AE types named in the text: succinylcholine-induced apnea, post-conditioning physiological disturbance (heart rate/muscle twitch/GSR), and four emetic-drug side effects (diarrhea, sinusitis, cystitis, prostatitis) plus neuromuscular disturbances.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Coded '.': no article-wide count of participants experiencing at least one AE is given; the only count present is n=15 for the apnea-duration statistic, not for AE incidence overall.
article.AE_denominator: Coded 'Not numbered': the AEs are drawn from a narrative synthesis of several different reviewed sources with different sample sizes (e.g., the succinylcholine physiological data come from a 15-patient pilot study, while the emetic-drug side-effect list cites no denominator at all); no single assessed population size applies to the set as a whole.
article.ArmScope: Coded 'NA': the AE data are pooled narratively across multiple distinct non-trial sources (a 15-patient succinylcholine pilot study and an unspecified emetic-drug literature) rather than drawn from one trial's exposed arm(s), so neither 'psychedelic_arm' nor 'pooled' cleanly applies; this is a genuine case where arm scope does not apply rather than merely a single-arm study.
article.WorstSeverity: Coded 'Moderate': the maximum Severity among the seven ae_events is Moderate (succinylcholine apnea/paralysis, rubric-graded; and author-graded 'light to moderate' neuromuscular disturbances).

ae_events.Costello 1969_AE01: Apnea duration (mean 90.4s, SD 24s, range 63-150s) is reported for Sanderson, Campbell & Laverty's 15-patient succinylcholine pilot study (ref 27), relayed narratively by Costello rather than measured by him. Graded Moderate/rubric because respiratory paralysis is the deliberate, monitored unconditioned stimulus of the method (saline-drip access, three therapists present) and self-resolves within the reported duration, but the article gives no detail on clinical management or complications beyond duration, so SeverityIndeterminate=Y; a stricter reading of 'life-threatening' under FDA seriousness criteria could argue for Severe instead. NAffected=15 because the duration statistics are reported across the full pilot sample.
ae_events.Costello 1969_AE02: Irregular heart rate, muscle twitches and GSR-baseline fluctuation after the succinylcholine conditioning session are described qualitatively (ref 27) with no participant count or explicit severity grading; defaulted to Mild/rubric with SeverityIndeterminate=Y per the under-specified-AE rule.
ae_events.Costello 1969_AE03: The author's own text states emetic-drug diarrhea is 'mostly mild', a direct severity descriptor, so SeveritySource=author and SeverityIndeterminate=N despite no participant count being given.
ae_events.Costello 1969_AE04: Sinusitis is named in a summary list of emetic-drug side effects with no severity language or count anywhere in the text; defaulted to Mild/rubric with SeverityIndeterminate=Y.
ae_events.Costello 1969_AE05: Cystitis is named in the same summary list with no severity language or count; defaulted to Mild/rubric with SeverityIndeterminate=Y.
ae_events.Costello 1969_AE06: Prostatitis is named in the same summary list with no severity language or count; defaulted to Mild/rubric with SeverityIndeterminate=Y.
ae_events.Costello 1969_AE07: The author explicitly characterizes neuromuscular disturbances from emetic drugs as 'light to moderate'; the worst end of that stated range (Moderate) is used per the WorstSeverity/max-severity convention, so SeveritySource=author and SeverityIndeterminate=N.

config_proposal.metric: None (narrative review; no original effect size reported)
config_proposal.note: Review article with no original trial: the author conducted no prospective enrollment or intervention of his own. The six LSD studies and multiple aversion-therapy studies discussed each carry their own separately-extractable statistics rather than a single value belonging to this record, so no defensible conversion exists for this article itself.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Narrative synthesis of heterogeneous, partly conflicting primary studies (75% mean LSD improvement across largely uncontrolled comparisons vs. no LSD advantage over ephedrine/time in the one rigorously controlled study, Smart et al. 1966; 'no good evidence' that aversion therapy is particularly effective overall) with no single direction or magnitude attributable to this article's own analysis.
